I stopped round 201 before changing any code: one required token removal (R94) would leave a store control with no visible focus indicator. B needs to rule on it.

**The problem:** in `SfxVideoSync.tsx` (lines 34–40), the "Choose video" `<label>` wraps a file input that is invisible (`opacity-0`). Today the focus ring is drawn on the label by the two `focus-within:ring-*` tokens. R94 says to remove those. After that, the only indicator is the global outline on the input itself, and because the input is invisible, the outline is too. R97 only moves the ring's offset, so it can't fix this. That matches the task's own STOP rule.

**Measured in Chromium (a minimal copy of the label, not the real page):** after Tab, the input is focused and its outline is reported as "solid 1px", but nothing is drawn. Brass pixels around the control:
- with the current ring: 693
- with R94 applied: 69
- unfocused, for comparison: 69

The page that shows this control is `/scenes/:id`, which needs the backend and is blocked here, so I couldn't check it in the real app.

**Rest of the check:** I scanned all 27 sweep files for other hidden focusable elements. `SfxVideoSync` is the only one R94 would break. The two honeypot inputs aren't reachable by Tab, and the `hire-us` select is visible. The checkbox in `ExportDialog` and the URL field in `VideoUploadZone` will keep a visible ring, but I judged that from the code only. One separate issue that existed before this round: the hover-only play button overlay on product cards (`ProductCard.tsx:132`) can be tabbed to on wider screens, but its ring is already invisible. R94 doesn't touch it; B may want to record it.

**Ready for the re-dispatch:**
- Start checks pass: HEAD `5b1a2bb`, clean tree, 1001 frozen files, grant start hashes.
- The inventory matches B: 155 tokens in 31 files (store), 13 in 5 (Studio).
- The two CSS classes R95 removes the focus rules for are used nowhere else in `app/`.
- The hook in R93 can move to `root.tsx`, because that component renders on every route, Studio included.

**Options for B (detail in the report):**
- **(a)** Allow one `has-[:focus-visible]:` outline on that label, and adjust the new scanner test (STF2) and the after-count to accept it.
- **(b)** Allow restructuring the input so focus lands on something visible. This also needs an STF2 exception.
- **(c)** Accept it as a recorded Low. This conflicts with C's rule that a lost indicator is Medium (WCAG 2.4.7).
- **(d)** Keep the two tokens on this one label. The count becomes 17 tokens in 6 files, and this one spot keeps a shadow ring instead of the shared outline.

**What I didn't do:** no source files changed. I didn't create the new test file or doc 160. I ran no app tests, typecheck, lint or code review, because there was nothing to check. No B acceptance criterion past the start checks and the inventory is passed.

**For C:** run the short round from lesson L22: the scope/hash check and the auth guard (G201-3), then report "not implemented (A STOP)". The retro re-check (RT-FIX) doesn't depend on my work and can still run.
